author: Nico Martinez
title: Jalen Duren Agrees To $200 Million Deal With Pistons, Ending Prolonged Standoff - NewsBreak
text:
By Nico Martinez ,
56 minutes ago After a long and chaotic free agency, the Jalen Duren saga is finally over in Detroit. According to ESPN’s Shams Charania, the 22-year-old big man has just agreed to a five-year, $200 million contract that will keep him with the team through 2030.
As a restricted free agent this summer, Duren was holding out in hopes of securing a full five-year max deal worth $287 million. But as the summer progressed, the Pistons never budged, resulting in a stalemate that dragged on for months. Now, finally, it seems he has settled on the Pistons’ standing proposal, which equates to roughly $40 million per year.

“ All-NBA and All-Star center Jalen Duren has agreed to sign a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons. Duren ultimately accepts the standing Pistons proposal ahead of the 11:59 pm ET deadline on a one-year, $9.6M qualifying offer,” reported Shams Charania on Thursday . “Detroit placed the $200M guaranteed offer two weeks ago after offers ranging from $170M to $190M throughout the summer. There were fractures built within the player-team relationship during the business of restricted free agency that impact the start of the Pistons season. The 22-year-old skipped media day and the start of training camp mulling over the QO and hoping for a potential sign and trade, but the Pistons stood firm, awaiting a decision, and the sides lock-in long-term on a massive deal.”
The news comes after months of dramatic and brutal negotiations. After helping the Pistons to the first seed last season, with averages of 19.5 points, 10.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 0.8 steals, and 0.8 blocks per game on 65.0% shooting from the field, Duren felt he should get paid like a franchise star, on par with some of the best players in the game. So when the Pistons tried to get him to accept a pay cut, he didn’t take it very well. It only made it worse when they signed Duren’s teammate, Ausar Thompson , to a $155 million deal .
By all accounts, Duren became disillusioned with the franchise over what he considered a “disrespectful” offer . There were even reports that he could take the qualifying offer and join the Kings next summer, who are reportedly willing and ready to offer a full max deal. In the end, however, Duren decided to stay in Detroit and finish what he started after being drafted in 2022.
It was a chaotic and oftentimes ugly standoff, but it ended in a way that might just save the Pistons’ trajectory. Without Duren, they had no hope of competing for the title or staying relevant in the East. But with the star big man committed for another five years, they are poised to be in contention for the foreseeable future. What’s important is that the drama is finally over, freeing the Pistons of any distractions or impending doom about their current situation. Now, with Duren for sure coming back (as head coach J.B. Bickerstaff always knew he would), they can continue their plan of building up around Cade Cunningham and bringing the championship back to Detroit for the first time since 2004.
